title: Add a pricing tier without editing Pricer

task.text: Each new customer tier means editing the `switch` in `Pricer`.

Make `Pricer` closed for modification: a new tier must be a new rule that is registered, not a new `case`. `Pricing.price(tier, cents)` must keep returning exactly what it returns now, including full price for unknown tiers.

items: Add `interface PriceRule` with one method, `long apply(long cents)`.
`Pricer(Map<String, PriceRule>)` keeps `long price(String tier, long cents)`.
Define VIP, STAFF and CLEARANCE as rules outside `Pricer`: `Tiers.standard()` returns them as a `Map<String, PriceRule>`.

checks.title: VIP and STAFF prices are unchanged
Pricer accepts a tier it has never seen
Pricer knows no tier; Tiers.standard() does

hints.text: What changes monthly is the set of tiers, and what stays is "look up a rule, apply it". Name the rule, then make `Pricer` know only that name.
Give `Pricer` a `Map<String, PriceRule>` through its constructor. `Pricer.price` finds the rule and applies it. The three tiers move to `Tiers.standard()`, and `Pricing` wires them together.
